learning_outcomes.text: Be able to apply calculation methods for articulated bar structures to determine the stress and deformation state in specific articulated systems.
Be able to apply the matrix method for calculating bar structures in specific structural systems.
Be able to implement simple bar structure models and calculate their static response to external actions using commercial structural calculation software tools.
Be able to prepare technical reports and documents in the field of structural analysis.
Be able to formulate and solve the equations governing the static response of articulated bar structures subjected to external actions.
Be able to formulate and solve the matrix equations governing the static behavior of a structure subjected to external actions.
Be able to determine internal forces in bar structure elements and size them based on mechanical resistance and stiffness requirements.

syllabus_topics: BLOC I: BASES DE CÀLCUL I ACCIONS
TEMA 2. CÀLCUL D'ACCIONS EN ESTRUCTURES INDUSTRIALS
Actions, structural safety and regulatory framework
Calculation of actions according to CTE DB SE-AE
The structural model (coord. systems, nodes, dof, elements, element properties, boundary conditions, actions, action combinations)
Model variables: internal force and displacement vectors
Degree of hyperstaticity of planar articulated structures
Calculation of axial forces in planar articulated structures
Principle of virtual work applied to planar articulated structures
Stiffness matrix of an element in local coordinates
Stiffness matrix of rigid element in global coordinates.
Structure level equation in global coordinates. Assembly
Application of boundary conditions: nodal solution
Stiffness matrix of an articulated bar
Method summary and extrapolation to three dimensions
Buckling length with non-biarticulated boundary conditions
TEMA 7. INTRODUCCIÓ A L'ANÀLISI DINÀMICA D'ESTRUCTURES
Single degree of freedom systems in free vibration
Single degree of freedom systems in forced vibration
PROB1) Actions in a contributed industrial warehouse
PROB2) Calculation of forces and displacements in a planar articulated structure.
PROB3) Matrix calculation of planar structures
PROB4) Buckling calculation of slender elements
PROB5) Dynamic calculation of a planar structure
LAB1) Obtaining actions using computer software
LAB2) Static analysis of planar articulated structures with computer software
LAB4) Analysis of planar structures with rigid nodes using computer software
LAB4) Buckling analysis of a planar structure with computer software
LAB5) Dynamic analysis of a bridge with computer software
teaching_methods: Lectures (for theoretical foundations, supported by multimedia presentations and blackboard)
Problem and exercise solving (interspersed with theoretical explanations, simple examples by professor, short examples by students, discussion)

Laboratory work (practical sessions, some in structures lab, others in computer lab using software for problem solving. Experimental measurements of forces, stresses, deformations, displacements. Autonomous work with professor assistance, requiring reports.)

assessment_methods.method: Completion and delivery of laboratory practical works
Continuous assessment activities, such as problem submissions and questionnaires

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain at least 5 out of 10 points in the overall average grade. In the first and second calls, the final exam (70% or 85%) requires a minimum grade of 4.5 out of 10; if this or any other minimum is not met, the overall grade cannot exceed 4.5. Continuous assessment activities include laboratory practical works (15%, not recoverable) and other activities like problems and questionnaires (15%, recoverable in the second call). The extraordinary call consists of a 100% final exam with no minimum grade; this call is consumed upon request. Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a 0 for that activity/exam and may lead to further sanctions.
